FINDING 1 -- #1 is already contradicted by this run's own history, and is unenforceable as written. #1 says an iteration submitted for requirement 0 SHALL be validated by an automated Android emulator test before that iteration can be marked succeeded. Iteration 15 IS an iteration submitted for requirement 0 and it IS marked succeeded (ok), while devsystem.android_emulator_test has 0 iterations and no such test exists. Either the gate is already broken, or "succeeded" does not mean what #1 assumes -- and it does not: on this platform succeeded records whether the iteration's own work was completed, not whether the requirement is met. Iteration 15 is exactly that case, an honest review that succeeded at reporting requirement 0 is NOT met. #1 conflates the two, so no implementation can satisfy it without redefining succeeded for every stage in the run. Recommend #1 be rewritten to gate requirement 0's VERIFICATION (confirmation of its acceptance criteria) on the emulator test, rather than gating any iteration's succeeded flag. Not fixed here: rewriting a requirement is devsystem.plan's job, not review's.

FINDING 2 -- #2 and #3 restate each other's criteria but assume two different, mutually exclusive architectures. Both demand end-to-end encryption of a 1:1 message under a per-session key no intermediary can derive; #2 c1/c2 and #3 c1/c2/c3 are near-restatements of one another. Their system models differ, though: #2 is written against the CADS-Tunnel broker plus :443-relay topology, where the intermediary only forwards ("neither the broker nor any relay hop can read or tamper"), while #3 c3/c4 assume a backend that STORES ciphertext and QUEUES a message for an offline recipient ("the server stores ciphertext only", "does not require the recipient to be online"). The path shipped today is direct peer-to-peer with no store-and-forward at all, so #3 c4 cannot be met by it even in principle, and nothing anywhere in this run records which of the two architectures was chosen. A reviewer therefore cannot verify either requirement, no matter what gets implemented. Recommend: decide store-and-forward yes/no first, then either merge #2 and #3 into one encryption requirement plus a separate offline-delivery requirement, or explicitly scope #2 to the transport hop and #3 to queued/at-rest state.

FINDING 3 -- #3 may already be partly satisfied by shipped code that no iteration has ever claimed. Iteration 15 reports a real, hermetically tested Noise_IK direct peer-to-peer session in native-bridge (ct_common::a2a, genuine AEAD-authenticated handshake, real encrypted TextMessage exchange). If that report is accurate, #3's criteria 1-3 are plausibly already substantially met for the direct-address path, yet #3 shows 0/4 and "not yet addressed by any iteration" purely because nobody ever claimed it. I am deliberately NOT confirming those criteria: I did not read that code myself in this iteration, and a review must not verify a requirement from another iteration's prose. Flagged so the next devsystem.android_native_bridge iteration claims #3 explicitly instead of leaving real work invisible to this run's own coverage.

FINDING 4 -- #4 is the only sensible next implementation target. Of the uncovered requirements, #1 needs a rewrite (finding 1), #2 and #3 need an architecture decision first (finding 2), and #5 is blocked by this platform having no artifact channel at all. #4 (real per-message sent/delivered/read status, an honest error state on failure, live updates without manual refresh) depends on none of those: it is app-local UI over the existing message path, and all 5 of its criteria are checkable on one device pair without downloading any artifact. Recommend it as the next bounded increment.

FINDING 1 -- (a) CANNOT BE DONE: a requirement is immutable once created. There is no edit path and no delete path for a requirement, or for one of its acceptance criteria, anywhere in this system. Verified three independent ways, not assumed:
- This control panel's Requirements panel renders exactly three interactive controls per requirement -- requirement-toggle (the overall verified flag), criterion-toggle (per acceptance criterion) and requirement-auto-judge-toggle -- plus a read-only "decision basis" disclosure. - devsystem.assistant is not a workaround: the only requirement verbs in its action vocabulary as used by this client are ToggleRequirement and ToggleAcceptanceCriterion. It has the same two toggles and nothing else.

This is an asymmetry rather than a deliberate immutability guarantee: this same platform lets you edit AND remove a custom panel, update AND remove a next-step draft, remove an indexed RAG document, and DELETE an entire run. A requirement -- the one object the mandatory review gate actually keys on, and what the coverage and N/M-confirmed counters score -- is the only load-bearing thing here that can never be corrected.

FINDING 2 -- (b) DECIDED: this run assumes a forwarding-only topology with NO ciphertext-storing backend. The decision is forced by what exists in this run, not by preference:
- The role set (plan, android_native_bridge, document_extraction, android_emulator_test, review, android_native_build_ci) contains no backend or server role. Nobody in this run owns a service that could hold a mailbox.
- repo_url is https://github.com/scimbe/CADS-webconference-android -- a client repo. There is no server repo in this run.
- Milestone M1 (achieved) is a direct CADS-Tunnel Noise_IK channel with history persisted LOCALLY. Milestone M2 -- the operator's own named next goal -- is ct-agent channel join, SignedChannelGrant, rendezvous, NAT traversal, :443 relay fallback. Every one of those is connection establishment or forwarding; none of them stores a message.
- Requirement #0 names that same mechanism, and #2 is written against that same topology ("neither the CADS-Tunnel broker nor any :443 relay hop can read or tamper").
- The backlog's open discovery item describes the broker as something a client JOINS to reach a peer, living in ct-agent/ct_edge -- not a message store.
DECISION OF RECORD FOR THIS RUN: forward-only, no store-and-forward. Messages transit; nothing queues them. #2 is this run's real encryption requirement.

CONSEQUENCE FOR #3, stated plainly because it is not recoverable: #3 c1 and c2 (on-device encryption before transmission; a fresh per-conversation session key via authenticated key exchange) describe the same property #2 c2 does and are satisfiable by the shipped Noise_IK mechanism -- iteration 18 finding 3 is right that these may already be substantially met on the direct-address path and were simply never claimed. #3 c3 ("the server stores ciphertext only") can only ever be vacuously true: there is no server, and a reviewer cannot confirm a property of a component that does not exist. #3 c4 ("does not require the recipient to be online; a queued message is encrypted before upload") is UNSATISFIABLE under this decision, by construction and permanently -- and per finding 1 it cannot be edited out. #3 can therefore never reach 4/4. Note also that #3 reads in a different vocabulary from the rest of this run -- "participant", "the server", "upload", "backend", where #0 and #2 say "Android client", "broker", "relay hop". It looks like a generic messenger requirement imported from a different system model, and that mismatch is the actual root of the #2/#3 conflict iteration 18 found.
